title: Two tasks each add 1. What's the total?
hook: Both threads add 1 to a counter that starts at 0. What does it end at?

doesNotKnow: that two tasks can overwrite each other's updates

misconception: Two tasks each adding 1 to a counter always give 2.
objective: The learner can say that adding 1 is three steps (read, add, write), so when two threads interleave their steps the counter can end at 1, not 2, and that locks keep the steps from interleaving.

claims.text: If A reads, B reads, then A adds and writes, then B adds and writes, both read 0 and both write 1, so the counter ends at 1.
claims.source: Node script running the six steps in that order with a private register per thread: counter = 1. Demo.tsx runs the same function it draws. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): node, own interpreter with a private register per thread: order A,B,A,A,B,B ends at 1 (both read 0, both write 1).

claims.text: If one thread finishes before the other starts, the counter ends at 2.
claims.source: Node script: order A,A,A,B,B,B gives 2. Of all 20 interleavings of the two three-step threads, 2 end at 2 and 18 end at 1. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): node: A,A,A,B,B,B ends at 2; of all 20 interleavings 2 end at 2 and 18 at 1.

claims.text: Adding 1 to a counter is three steps for each thread: read, add 1, write.
claims.source: Silberschatz, Galvin, Gagne, Operating System Concepts, chapter on process synchronization (race condition on count++, compiled to load, increment, store). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): Silberschatz, Galvin, Gagne, Operating System Concepts, process synchronization chapter: count++ as load, increment, store (race condition example).

claims.text: A lock keeps another thread from stepping in the middle of the three steps, which is why locks exist.
claims.source: Silberschatz et al., Operating System Concepts: mutual exclusion locks protect a critical section. Wording kept narrow: a lock prevents this interleaving, it is not the only reason locks exist. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): Mutual-exclusion lock around the critical section prevents the A,B interleaving (Silberschatz et al.). The stage's 'which is why locks exist' reads as a reason, not the only one.

claims.text: Each thread keeps its own copy of the value it read (shown as 'copy'); the stage also lists the steps in the order they ran.
claims.source: In the model each thread reads the counter into a private register or local variable before adding; stated in the build note as an idealised model. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): Demo.tsx run(): reg[t] is per thread; stage shows 'holds' from st.reg[t]. · Fact-check pass 19 2026-10-14: Demo.tsx run(): reg[t] is per thread, shown as 'copy' in each lane; 'Order run:' line from orderText(seq) lists steps in run order. Own node: run(A,B,A,A,B,B) = 1, run(A,A,A,B,B,B) = 2.

recall.question: A counter is 5. Threads A and B each read it, add 1 and write it back. Both read before either writes. What is the counter?
recall.why: Both read 5, both write 6. One update is lost, so the counter is 6, not 7.
